subject: Day 76: move swim off the waitlist
bodyText:
Today's focus
At about 3 months Avi is now age-eligible for parent-baby swim. Today is the day to convert the waitlist you joined back in week 4 into a booked first class.

Action items
- Move swim from the waitlist to a booked first parent-baby class now that he is around 3 months. Choose a warm-pool program with parent-in-water format rather than any independent-float gimmick. AAP HealthyChildren, swim lessons: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-play/Pages/Swim-Lessons.aspx
- Set up a childcare backup before you need it; identify a backup nanny agency or a family member on call so a sick nanny or closed daycare does not strand a workday.
- Inquire about first-birthday venues now if you plan to host; top Bay Area and NYC venues book 6 to 9 months out.
- Keep building the freezer milk stash at one to two pump sessions a day, aiming for roughly 2 oz frozen per missed feed, so the return-to-work handoff is not rushed.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Profuse drooling and hand-sucking now; this is salivary-gland maturation, not necessarily teething, since first teeth typically arrive at 6 to 10 months.
- [monitor] No reliable social smile yet, or a head that persistently turns to one side; document it for the 4-month visit.
- [call within 24h] Decreased feeding over 24 hours, or a new feeding-refusal pattern with no obvious cause.
- [call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, apnea, blue lips, or labored breathing is a same-day call, and 911 immediately for blue lips or breathing trouble!

Enrichment opportunities
- Book the first parent-baby swim class; at this age the value is sensory and social, with warm water and your face close, not any swimming skill. AAP HealthyChildren, swim lessons: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-play/Pages/Swim-Lessons.aspx
- Keep daily reading at 15 to 20 minutes with a roughly 3-to-1 repeat-to-novel ratio; repetition of favorites drives the predictive language processing that underwrites later vocabulary. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Answer his squeaks and squeals as if they were words, pausing for his turn before you reply; this serve-and-return cadence predicts stronger later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 84-91: sleep consolidation window opens (~3 months); start the consistent sleep-wake routine ahead of the 4-month shift
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit; vaccines RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2
- Weeks 14-18: 4-month sleep regression for many as night wakings increase

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
